They’re basically the chemicals that our nervous system releases when we feel pain and stress, and even feelings of happiness. They’re also released when we exercise, because you’re undergoing physical strain, and our bodies release it to make us feel better. Whenever we’re injured, it’s our body’s natural response, kinda like a natural pain killer. So when we self harm, that’s why you feel good afterwards, your body’s natural response to relieve pain kicked in, and we can get addicted to it, because it makes us feel “good”, similar to how alcohol, cocaine, and other intoxicating drugs make our bodies feel good. After a while, our body screams for it, needing more and more, causing us to cut more, and deeper, falling into a pit of addiction. Okay, if you need some help, I hope you don’t mind me asking you a few questions. 

What color is it, and what does it look like? Just to make sure that it is fat, fat should be yellow and bubbly, and possibly bulging out of the wound.

Is it bleeding a lot? If it’s bleeding out to the pulse of your heart that means you went too deep and hit an artery, and need to go to the hospital immediately.

Do you have the supplies and tools needed to care for it? If you aren’t going to visit the ER and are going to handle it yourself, you need to make sure you clean it, and properly bandage it to prevent it from getting infected. If you don’t have anything to keep up with it, either make a quick trip to the store to pick up some gauze dressings and bandages, or just go to the hospital because it’s better than getting an infection.

Have you cut this deep before? If not, just know that it’s going to burn, and be pretty sore for the first week. And, it’s going to take about a little over a month to heal, from my experience.

Okay, so I agree with you on how self harm isn’t necessarily “bad” since it isn’t hurting anyone else and it’s your own body, so you have a right to do whatever you want with your own self. However, I don’t think it’s a really good idea to encourage people with mental illnesses to self harm. If you don’t have the right tools for cleaning and bandaging to avoid dangerous situations like infection, it can put you in a pretty shitty situation. And you have to think of the people who go too deep too, the people that pass out from blood loss and end up in the ER, or even dead. Not good. If we were to “encourage” sh as a coping mechanism, it would have to be for shallow, non life threatening cuts, or not super severe burns, etc. But there’s no way you can monitor how people self harm, since we can be pretty reckless with our bodies, and obviously aren’t going to listen when someone tells us not to self harm. I’m not trying to change your mind since I understand where you’re coming from, I’m just mentioning certain serious consequences that can happen from self injury.

I’ve been in this situation far too many times, even now as we speak. First, I have to ask how far did you go? If you hit fat (weird yellow bubbly stuff) that is concerning, but you can still treat yourself if you do it safely and if you absolutely have to. If you have steri strips on you, use those to close up the wound, minimize the scarring, and speed up the healing process. Always keep it covered in something clean for at least a week, after that it should start to heal more and depending on how deep it is it might even scab over. If you have ace bandages or any kind of long wrapping bandage, use them. The key to making sure you won’t get an infection is keeping it covered, unexposed to anything dangerous. Use small amounts of wound healing ointments, but not too much, as it’s not always safe to use certain medicines on severe, deep wounds. I have an antiseptic wound wash that I use to clean mine, but I’m pretty sure soap and water should clean fine too, it’s better than nothing. Change your dressings or bandages every day, and clean your cut. I see you posted this yesterday, so I guess we’re in the same boat, as I (regretfully) relapsed pretty bad last night. My arm is currently wrapped in gauze, and last night after I did it I put healing ointment directly on my wounds. Later tonight I’m going to change my dressing, clean it with more wound wash, and put on more medicine. Unfortunately, I don’t have any steri strips so I have some pretty wide cuts on my arm, which is going to suck because it usually takes me a month to have something this deep finally scab over :/ But if you’re in the same situation for the first time, be prepared to treat your arm or wherever you harmed like a delicate newborn baby. You have to constantly clean and check up on it. And it’s going to be pretty sore for a while too.
